description: Diagnose Linux latency, CPU, I/O, syscall and scheduling problems by writing small, bounded bpftrace programs after forming a hypothesis, with explicit checks for kernel support (BTF, kernel version), privileges (root or CAP_BPF/CAP_PERFMON), probe stability and tracing overhead. Use when top/strace/perf are not enough and you need per-event or per-latency evidence from a live Linux host, for example "what is opening these files", "why is read latency spiky", "which process causes block I/O". Not for first-line triage (use linux-troubleshooting), for CPU flame-graph profiling workflows (use performance-profiling), nor for macOS/Windows, nor for writing production eBPF programs in C/Rust (libbpf, Aya) or security enforcement.
